chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

A man prayed two rakʿahs of the obligatory prayer, then gave salām while thinking that he had completed the prayer, and he spoke. Then he remembered that he had not prayed two rakʿahs, so he عليه السلام said: He should complete what remains of his prayer, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.فَسَلَّمَ: he ended the prayer with salām
key_terms.وَتَكَلَّمَ: he spoke after assuming the prayer was over
key_terms.وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no penalty or blame upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone speaks after mistakenly thinking an obligatory prayer is finished, then remembers rakʿahs are still missing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who mistakenly ends an obligatory salat (prayer) early and speaks, believing the prayer was complete. If he later remembers that two rakʿahs remain, he should complete the rest of the prayer and no liability is upon him.
